Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Seaborn), Maya Chen (ML Eng - Seaborn), Sara Ali (Product)

Auto-generated summary:
Seaborn Systems is evaluating Redwood for an initial pilot focused on multilingual customer support and internal knowledge retrieval. Key evaluation dimensions: model selection (open models vs hosted variants), context length (up to 64k tokens in long-ticket workflows), tool-calling / retrieval integration, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and security controls (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Redwood AE/SE to send sizing/pricing and benchmark guide; customer to provide sample flows and compliance contacts.

Topics:
- Model comparisons: open models (Mistral, MPT variants), Redwood-verified variants vs hosted API
- Context length needs: multi-doc threads, 32k-64k token experiments
- Multilingual support: English + Spanish + French + Japanese requirements
- Tool-calling & retrieval: vector DB integration, function calling, structured outputs
- Deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data residency

Transcript:
00:00 Evan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh hey Liam, Maya, Sara from Seaborn, good to see you. quick intro - I'm Evan, AE on the infra team, and Priya's our solutions engineer.
00:10 Liam: hey thanks, yeah we appreciate it. we're, um, evaluating options for our support automation and knowledge base assistant. main levers are accuracy in multi-turns, long context, and multilingual.
00:20 Priya: great, thanks. can I ask what your current stack looks like for retrieval and embeddings?
00:28 Maya: sure, right now we store docs in a vector DB (Pinecone-ish) and use an in-house embedding pipeline. retrieval latency's okay but the model side is the bottleneck - we need consistent 200-400ms token latency for live chat and lower cost for nightly batch processing.
00:45 Evan: understood. on model selection — are you leaning toward hosted managed endpoints or more control with Dedicated/Private?
00:52 Liam: security is a big part. for the pilot we'd be fine with hosted, but long-term we expect Dedicated or VPC private for data residency. we need to know the gap in latency/cost between modes.
01:05 Priya: good, that matches typical customers. a few clarifying Qs: what's your target context window for the heaviest flows? you mentioned long threads?
01:15 Maya: yeah for some support tickets we need to feed entire thread + attachments, so sometimes we're talking 50k tokens, maybe up to 64k in extreme cases. most flows are 4-8k though.
01:28 Priya: okay that pushes into the long-context models or chunked retrieval with KV/prefix caching. Redwood supports both approaches - we can host long-context open models and we also provide KV cache to keep prefixes resident in memory to avoid re-decoding. that reduces cost and latency.
01:45 Sara: what's the tradeoff between running a long-context model vs chunking with retrieval? is accuracy hit?
01:52 Priya: typically chunking + rerank works well for factual retrieval, but for generative summarization of long threads a true long-context model preserves more coherence. cost-wise long-context models are pricier per token, Dedicated helps amortize that with reserved GPU throughput.
02:10 Liam: how about models — which open models do you recommend for multilingual and tool calling? we need Spanish and Japanese support.
02:18 Evan: we usually recommend testing a small set: Mistral-derived 8k/32k variants for cost-sensitive flows, and specifically verified Redwood long-context variants (we call them r-lg-* internally) for 64k needs. For multilingual, some community models are strong, but we also benchmark Anthropic-ish and OpenAI if customers consider hybrid strategy.
02:36 Maya: are the Redwood variants quantized? we want to run on Dedicated with 8-bit to save cost, but worried about quality drop.
02:43 Priya: yes we have quantization profiles per model. for many tasks int8/llm.int8 is a good trade; we run evaluation side-by-side. the Optimize tool will recommend quant levels based on your eval set.
02:58 Liam: tool-calling is critical. we need function calls to our internal ticketing API and structured JSON outputs. does that work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
03:07 Priya: yes, function-calling and structured outputs are supported on all deployment modes. Hosted provides easiest onboarding with rate-limits and streaming; Dedicated has isolated endpoints and lower jitter. For Private we integrate with your VPC and can route calls to internal tooling behind firewall.
03:25 Maya: latency specifics — if we aim for 200-400ms per token for live, what hardware profile do you recommend?
03:34 Evan: for that SLO you'd look at A100 or H100 class. On Dedicated we size GPU pools and set autoscaling policies; throughput and batching preferences affect per-token latency. we can provide a sizing worksheet.
03:46 Sara: what about fallback strategies if Dedicated is saturated? we need graceful degradation.
03:51 Priya: Redwood's smart routing supports fallbacks to lower-cost, higher-latency model variants or multi-region routing. you can set policies per-route, e.g., prioritize latency for live chat and cost for batch.
04:05 Liam: curious about cost estimation — e.g., if we run 1k concurrent users during peak with 50k-token flows, how do you model that?
04:13 Evan: we'll need sample qps and average tokens/session; that's why the worksheet helps. we also show unit economics: token cost, GPU amortization for Dedicated, and caching gains for repeated prefixes.
04:24 Maya: ok we'll get those numbers. on security, do you support KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys for Private?
04:31 Priya: yes, Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations and audit logs. Hosted offers envelope encryption and can integrate with cloud KMS; Dedicated and Private allow more direct control. we also maintain SOC2 reports and can provide compliance materials.
04:45 Liam: great. another question: how stable are model behaviors across updates? we need to avoid regressions in our LLM outputs for NLU tasks.
04:54 Priya: Redwood has model versioning and rollouts; you can pin versions, do canary rollouts and automatic fallback if a new variant causes regressions. we tie regressions to prompt sets/evals in the console.
05:06 Sara: for the POC, we'd like to run multilingual tests and a long-context summarization benchmark. timeline?
05:14 Evan: recommended POC is 2-3 weeks: week 0 setup and dataset upload, week 1 benchmarks and tuning, week 2 integration tests + ops validation. we can start the week of 2027-03-28 pending paperwork.
05:25 Liam: any blockers on your side for connecting to our vector DB and sample data?
05:31 Priya: we'll need a service account with read-only access to the test vector indices and an example embedding spec. for Hosted it's straightforward; Dedicated/Private we'll discuss private peering.
05:44 Maya: one more technical: do you support incremental KV caching for chat contexts so we don't resend entire history?
05:50 Priya: yes, Redwood's runtime supports KV cache management and prefix caching to keep recent tokens in memory. that reduces repeated compute for long chat histories.
06:00 Evan: recap — action items: I will send the Dedicated sizing worksheet and indicative pricing, Priya will share the benchmark guide and sample prompt set, Seaborn will send sample flows and token/QPS estimates, and Seaborn to confirm security contacts.
06:12 Liam: sounds good. thanks, Evan, Priya. we'll aim to review the materials and confirm the POC kickoff.
06:18 Evan: perfect. I'll follow up by Wednesday. thanks everyone.
